names.es: Alioli Casero con Yema de Huevo

metadata.notes: Sibling of handmade-alioli.json (see that file's metadata.comparisonGroup) — same tools (knife only for PEEL, everything else mortar-only), same peel -> salt -> crush(fine_paste) opening sequence on garlic-1, same EMULSIFY action and target. Two differences, both deliberate: (1) an extra step, SEPARATE on egg-1 (data/actions/separate.json), producing egg_yolk-1 (used) plus egg_white-1/egg_shell-1 (spawned, unused here — same 'leftover byproduct just sits in inventory' pattern as potato_peel in salted-fried-potatoes.json); only the yolk goes in, matching real technique (egg white would thin/loosen the emulsion, not stabilize it). (2) emulsify's params: oilAdditionRate 'slow_stream' (not 'drop_by_drop') and durationSeconds 240 (4 minutes, not 900/15) — lecithin's greater stabilizing power (egg_yolk.json's isEmulsionStabilizer) means real technique tolerates faster pouring and finishes far quicker than the egg-free version. Both numbers are directly comparable to handmade-alioli.json's for exactly that reason: same parameter ids, same units, different values, not a different modeling approach.
metadata.honestyNote: egg_yolk-1's presence in the emulsify step's availableIngredientInstanceIds does not itself change engine behavior — requiredIngredientCapabilities still only checks isEmulsifier (satisfied by oil-1, unchanged from handmade-alioli.json). The faster/more-forgiving outcome this recipe represents lives entirely in the chosen parameter VALUES (oilAdditionRate/durationSeconds), authored to reflect real technique, not derived by the engine from egg_yolk-1 being on hand — see egg_yolk.json's emulsionStabilizerNote and emulsify.json's patienceNote for the same limitation stated elsewhere.
